findings.title: Environment test never proves secret values stay out of retained artifacts
findings.trigger: A prohibited control or provider secret is removed from the child environment but is copied into a worker spec, diagnostic, stdout/stderr, receipt, result, event journal, or verification log.
findings.impact: D1R-01 can pass its key-name capture while D1-AC01's explicit no-secret-value requirement remains false, leaving Primary credentials in durable local evidence.
findings.evidence: D1-AC01 requires that no secret values appear in packets, receipts, or logs, but D1R-01 and Narrow Verification specify only child env key-name capture and do not bind a canary scan over every retained artifact.
findings.suggestion: Inject unique non-production canary values for a Primary control key, an unrelated provider key, and the selected-Host auth path; assert required key delivery without printing the value, then byte-scan every generated spec/result/receipt/log/event/evidence artifact for absence of all canaries.

findings.title: Live Host smoke has no independent proof that denied probes were attempted and blocked
findings.trigger: The selected ZCode run simply follows the prompt without requesting a denied tool, or reports that a probe was denied even though no mechanical enforcement event occurred.
findings.impact: The planned receipt can claim D1Q-02 and qualify an unenforced Host path from absence of effects or Host self-report, allowing a later Worker to perform the very outside-root, shell, network, or business effect D1 must fail closed.
findings.evidence: The plan rejects Host self-report at line 19, yet the required receipt binds only general run and denied-probe observations; it does not require the exact probe-instruction digest, an observed permission/tool attempt, or coordinator-owned pre/post canaries for each denied dimension.
findings.suggestion: Bind the exact instruction and permission digests, require an independently observed attempt-and-denial event for every tool-mediated dimension, and use coordinator-owned isolated filesystem markers and a local controlled network sink for pre/post effect checks; an unattempted or unobservable probe must remain unsupported, not pass.

findings.title: Fence test does not cover physical-root aliases or overlapping roots
findings.trigger: Two delegation packets name the same writable tree through a symlink, Windows case or separator spelling, or parent/child root overlap while a literal-path fence treats them as different owners.
findings.impact: Both runs can acquire fences and write concurrently, violating the zero-duplicate-writer prerequisite even though the single duplicate-launch fixture passes.
findings.evidence: D1R-03 asks for one atomic duplicate-launch fixture and fence identity/readback evidence but does not enumerate the alias and overlap cases that bypass a string-keyed or exact-root-only fence.
findings.suggestion: Make the duplicate-launch check table-driven for exact worktree, parent/child writable-root overlap, symlink or filesystem alias, and Windows case/separator aliases, and assert that disjoint registered worktrees remain independently admissible.

findings.title: ACP conformance consumer is named but has no outcome_unknown fixture
findings.trigger: A delegation reaches launcher-side failure_type outcome_unknown and the ACP conformance receipt or diagnostic consumes that previously unseen value.
findings.impact: The focused suite can stay green while the maintained conformance surface misclassifies, drops, or leaks the new recovery fact; the full gate's existing happy-path test does not exercise this transition.
findings.evidence: Tech Notes explicitly require checking every failure_type consumer including ACP conformance, but the Planned Path Inventory and Narrow Verification include only delegate and ACP-driver tests, with no conformance-specific fixture.
findings.suggestion: Add one ACP conformance fixture that consumes outcome_unknown and asserts the retained redacted receipt and diagnostic, or record source evidence that the consumer is intentionally unchanged and already covered by an executable equivalent.

positive_observations: The plan correctly separates deterministic fake-child and nested-writer tests from the single live Host enforcement observation.
N=1 compatibility is backed by focused driver/delegation suites and the full release and package gates.
Unsupported Host enforcement remains a typed blocker instead of being converted into a permissive fallback.
limitations: This is a plan-only review; no D1 runtime diff, RED fixture, live ZCode smoke, or retained execution evidence exists yet.
